name: Matrei am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Wipptal valley, home to the Bergbauernmuseum and the starting point for hikes in the Tuxer Alpen.
beschreibung:
Matrei am Brenner is perched at an altitude of 992 meters at the gateway to the Wipptal valley, nestled between the craggy foothills of the Tux Alps to the west and the forested slopes of the Patscherkofel massif to the east. This historic market town of around 940 inhabitants looks back on an eventful history as an essential postal station along the historic Brenner Pass road, which carried merchants and travelers between North and South Tyrol for centuries. Even today, the steady rhythm of alpine transit along the Brenner railway and motorway subtly shapes the life of the valley.

In the village center, the Mountain Farming Museum (Bergbauernmuseum), housed in a carefully preserved historic farmhouse, offers fascinating insights into the arduous life of Tyrolean mountain farmers from the 18th century through the post-war era. Situated right on the banks of the Sill river, Matrei is an ideal base for mountain hikes into the Tux Alps, including ascents up the striking Serles peak or into the peaceful side valleys of Navis and Schmirn. In winter, the nearby Bergeralm ski area offers family-friendly slopes and wide panoramic views across the Wipptal.

The parish church of the Holy Cross with its distinctive steeple defines the skyline, alongside traditional taverns where hearty South Tyrolean dishes meet classic North Tyrolean hospitality. Those seeking serenity can follow the ancient packhorse trails leading towards Maria Waldrast, the historic pilgrimage site high above the valley floor.
